# Senior Systems Engineer — Disney Experiences

---
**Job ID:** 10161502
**Date Posted:** Nov 3, 2026
**Date Applied:** Nov 7, 2026
**Salary Range:** $113,500–$152,200 per year — Orlando, FL (role located in Lake Buena Vista, FL)
---

## Job Summary

A production-operations role in Disney Experiences (DX) technology that carries Warehouse Management Systems from implementation into sustained production. The Senior Systems Engineer covers go-live readiness, post-implementation stabilization, hypercare, and long-term operational ownership of newly delivered capabilities, and is a key point of contact for the Distribution Services teams across DX properties. The role is the subject-matter expert for the WMS and its ancillary systems, acting as liaison between business, vendors, and technology teams while supporting production operations, enhancements, and backlog prioritization. It reports to the Manager, Software Engineering.

---

## What You'll Do

- Be accountable for uptime, recoverability, and operational readiness of warehouse production systems.
- Own the health, stability, and performance of live production applications.
- Support implementation and go-live activities, ensuring systems are production-ready and supportable.
- Participate in an on-call rotation leading incident response, triage, and service recovery.
- Serve as the technical escalation point for complex production issues.
- Facilitate deep root cause analysis across application, integration, and infrastructure layers.
- Drive accountability for SLAs, feature delivery, release execution, and issue resolution with external vendors.
- Perform hands-on technical analysis when required to accelerate vendor troubleshooting and resolution.
- Create, maintain, and improve runbooks, diagnostics, and operational documentation.
- Balance short-term remediation with long-term system stability and operability improvements.
- Lead transition-to-support activities, including knowledge transfer, operational documentation, and stabilization following deployment.
- Develop and maintain configuration and asset records within ServiceNow.
- Proactively identify systemic risks and recurring issues and drive operational improvements.

### Required Qualifications
- Minimum of 5+ years of experience supporting large-scale, business-critical production systems
- Proven incident response and escalation leadership experience
- Strong troubleshooting skills across distributed systems
- Experience supporting vendor-provided or Commercial Off-the-Shelf platforms
- Ability to operate effectively under pressure during live production incidents
- Strong written communication skills for incident updates, executive communication, and postmortems
- Experience supporting cloud-hosted production systems on AWS, Azure, or GCP
- Demonstrated ability to drive resolution of complex, high-impact operational issues
- Comfortable diagnosing issues across compute, networking, storage, and system integrations
- Experience supporting Warehouse Management Systems or similarly complex, highly integrated Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) platforms
- Familiarity with Agile delivery practices
- Availability to work within a 24x7/365 schedule with advanced notice
- Preferred: hands-on experience supporting Blue Yonder Warehouse Management System in production; ITSM and ITIL-aligned service management models; ServiceNow or comparable service management tools; Scrum and Kanban environments using tools such as JIRA; driving accountability and corrective action through managed services vendor relationships; supporting supply chain, logistics, or warehouse operations environments

### Education
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a comparable field, or equivalent practical experience.

### Benefits
A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Nov 7, 2026

- **COTS platform and go-live experience is the strongest match:** Riley managed the Coplay location's Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central ERP implementation in five weeks, migrating more than 2,000 items and 150+ products, reconciling inventory on the floor, and syncing SKUs with Proteor's global locations. Riley then led the 2026 inventory count in Business Central, traced its discrepancies to production orders processed without verification, and helped implement a more warehouse-focused workflow. That is a vendor-provided platform carried through go-live, stabilization, and a root-cause-driven process fix in an inventory context, which is the shape of this role's WMS hypercare work.
- **Cloud-hosted COTS in production:** Proteor's Business Central is the online version, hosted by Microsoft on Azure and reached from any device off the company network (recorded in the [[Career Q&A Log]], Nov 7, 2026). Riley has supported a cloud-hosted SaaS ERP through go-live and into daily production, which partly answers the cloud requirement.
- **Other vendor platforms supported:** the ProteorPrintOS rollout on SimplyPrint (remote operation, AI-assisted diagnostics, live video, material and outcome metrics), Ubiquiti UniFi cloud gateways configured and monitored remotely across multiple sites, Allen Bradley PLCs, and, per the [[Career Q&A Log]], the Siemens PLCs on the filament extrusion lines, Duet3D controllers, and Mean Well power supplies. Riley describes vendor platforms and vendor work as day-to-day, regularly running into nights and early mornings. A self-developed ERP/CRM on a redundant Kubernetes cluster (Filament era) gives Riley the inside view of how an ERP's orders, inventory, and BOM data fit together, though it is custom-built rather than COTS.
- **Production ownership and troubleshooting:** ExtrusionStudio is live on all three filament extrusion lines since October 2026 and Riley owns it; Riley is the plant's technical subject-matter expert and the go-to contact for customer troubleshooting across mechanical faults, electrical faults, and user error. Network, VLAN, DNS, reverse-proxy, virtualization, and container administration in `skills.json` support the compute, networking, storage, and integration diagnosis requirement.
- **Written and executive communication:** monthly project status, constraints, and budget presentations at Proteor's USA review with global leadership; risk analysis and mitigation to EU and U.S. standards.
- **Gaps:** no AWS, Azure, or GCP administration is on the record; Business Central on Azure is SaaS that Microsoft operates, not infrastructure Riley administers. Siemens PLCs, Duet3D, and Mean Well are in the Q&A log but not yet on the site. No formal on-call rotation, incident-commander role, SLA-managed vendor relationship, or written postmortems are recorded, and the after-hours vendor work has no specific dated example yet. Nothing establishes Blue Yonder, ServiceNow, ITIL/ITSM, JIRA, or Scrum/Kanban. The production systems Riley supports are plant-scale, so "large-scale" in the posting's sense is the likeliest recruiter question; Riley's production support dates to May 2020 at Filament Innovations, which clears the 5+ year count.
- **Level:** the pay band and reporting line (Manager, Software Engineering) fit a senior individual-contributor move from Riley's Lead R&D role.

### Now — Nov 7, 2026

- **Vendor platforms now on the site (Nov 7, 2026):** Siemens PLCs, Duet3D controllers, and Mean Well power supplies were added to `skills.json` under Controls & Automation, closing the "in the Q&A log but not yet on the site" gap noted above. The cloud, on-call, and ITSM gaps are unchanged.
- **Production-readiness evidence (Nov 7, 2026):** the ExtrusionStudio project now records no unplanned outage during production since go-live and the packing-bench fix found during rollout, isolated layer by layer (frame rate, thermal throttling, a swapped Pi and SD card, a direct Ethernet run, display resolution). That partly answers "hands-on technical analysis" and root cause analysis across application, integration, and infrastructure layers. Per the [[Career Q&A Log]], Riley writes incident reports for leadership (not yet customers) and tracks work in GitHub and Kanban boards in Microsoft Teams, which touches the preferred Kanban item; Business Central serves the 10 to 15 people at the facility and 10 to 30 more at other Proteor locations. Still missing: an on-call rotation, an incident Riley led, SLA-managed vendors (the Business Central contact is Proteor headquarters, not a Microsoft partner), storage work, ServiceNow, JIRA, ITIL, and Blue Yonder.

## About the Company

The position is with Walt Disney Attractions Technology LLC, part of Disney Experiences (DX), whose technology team builds the digital and physical Guest experience for Disney Parks and Resorts worldwide, Disney Cruise Line, Aulani, and Disney Vacation Club, across Attractions and Entertainment, Food and Beverage, Resorts and Transportation, and Merchandise. This role supports the Distribution Services teams across DX properties. Lake Buena Vista is home to Disney Springs, Disney's Typhoon Lagoon Water Park, Disney's Lake Buena Vista Golf Course, and several resort hotels. The Walt Disney Company operates through three segments: Disney Entertainment, ESPN, and Disney Experiences.
